title: The energy an isolated half of a critical chain cannot give up
subtitle: Conformal amplitudes, dispersion, and the cost of conserving particle number
shortTitle: What entanglement locks away in a critical chain
oneLine: The bound energy of half a critical chain is (3v/2πc)·S²/L for conformal models and the hopping and Ising chains, but chains with the same ground state can follow different powers of L, and conserving particle number changes the power again
abstract: Cut a critical quantum chain in its ground state in two and isolate one half. Because the half is entangled with the rest, it holds energy above its own ground state; unitary operations on the half can extract most of it as work, but a remainder, the bound energy, always stays. Mula and colleagues (2023) found for the free-fermion hopping chain that the bound energy scales as the square of the entanglement entropy divided by the length, and conjectured this for critical chains in general. This candidate proves the law, with coefficient 3v/(2πc) (v the velocity, c the central charge), for a regulated boundary conformal field theory and directly for the open hopping and critical Ising lattice chains; at equal velocity the Ising slope is twice the hopping slope, so the conjectured number is not universal. For a family of free-fermion chains that all share the hopping chain's ground state, the bound energy is fixed by the flattest zero of the block's one-particle dispersion, and the S²/L form holds if and only if the dispersion crosses the Fermi level with nonzero velocity and has no other zero: criticality of the ground state does not determine the bound energy. In one range-three chain, unrestricted, particle-number-conserving and one-body operations leave residuals of orders (log L)³/L², (log L)/L and (log L)²/L. Limits: free-fermion chains and an idealised conformal model only (interacting chains such as the Heisenberg chain remain open); the lattice proofs use the known boundary Rényi asymptotics of the open hopping chain; operations are idealised; coefficients are limits in L and some converge only logarithmically. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 20-page paper with a context-first introduction, written proofs of all theorems, limits, open problems and an AI-use statement. Ten Python scripts (numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.17.0, mpmath 1.3.0, matplotlib 3.10.8) with recorded outputs: complete Fock-space orderings and direct many-body checks for small chains, an interval-arithmetic certificate of an ordering inversion at five sites, Ising spin and Majorana calculations, exact Ising boundary-character counts, the crossover quadrature, the pressure constants and quoted coefficients, and a finite-size table up to L = 4096. Every script exits with status 1 on failure, also under python -O. These finite calculations test values, constants and identities; they do not certify the asymptotic theorems. A clean replay in optimised mode reproduced the recorded outputs (identical except final digits of one floating-point file); changing the expected D_3 makes the dispersion check fail. Linux CI reruns all ten, comparing the exact certificate and integer counts byte for byte and floating-point outputs within declared relative tolerances (1e-6; 1e-3 for the finite-size table, whose last printed digit of the cubic chain's one-body ratio is platform-sensitive).

keyResults: Lemma 1 (proof): under stated hypotheses the bound energy Q_L equals, to leading order, the energy of the block's thermal state whose entropy equals the entanglement entropy S_L.

Theorems 3–4 and Corollary 5 (proof): for a regulated boundary conformal field theory Q_L ~ 3v S_L²/(2πc L), whatever boundary condition the cut carries; in rational CFTs the next term is fixed by the boundary entropy.

Theorem 6 and Corollaries 7–8 (proof): every sign-preserving polynomial f gives a chain with the hopping ground state and Q_L ~ D(m, A) S_L^(m+1)/L^m, m the largest order of a zero of the dispersion; L Q_L/S_L² has a positive finite limit if and only if f′(0) ≠ 0 and f has no other zero on [−2, 2].
Corollary 9 (proof): for the critical Ising chain N Q/S² → 12/π, against 6/π for unit hopping (slopes 6/π and 3/π in units of L).

Theorems 10–14 (proof): a linear term restores the S²/L law through an explicit crossover; in the range-three chain f(x) = x(x − 3/2)² unrestricted, number-conserving and one-body controls leave residuals of orders (log L)³/L², (log L)/L and (log L)²/L.

Credit and limits: the conjecture and free-fermion formula are due to Mula et al.; free-fermion chains and an idealised conformal model only; one external input (boundary Rényi asymptotics); coefficients are limits in L, some approached logarithmically slowly (cubic chain at L = 4096: 36.3 against 11.2, one-body penalty 1.096 against 2.148).

decisionObject.description: Decide whether the bound energy of half a critical chain follows the conjectured S²/L law, with which coefficient, which data of the chain fix it, and how restricting the allowed operations changes it.
decisionObject.scope: Regulated boundary conformal field theory spectra; open free-fermion chains with one-particle Hamiltonian f(T) for sign-preserving polynomials f; the critical Ising chain; unrestricted, particle-number-conserving and one-body number-conserving unitaries on the block.
